runs.summary: Data through Aug 26 (Q3 partial). Top 3: SMH +54.3%, XLE +41.5%, XBI +38.2%. SPY P/E: 28.00x (up from 26.82x)
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: SMH +54.3% (P/E 44.89x, Expensive), XLE +41.5% (20.02x, Fair), XBI +38.2% (P/E N/A), CIBR +31.4% (38.16x, Expensive), XLK +27.3% (39.32x, Expensive).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XLC -3.8% (15.50x, Fair), XLY -1.5% (30.94x, Elevated), XLU +3.3% (21.64x, Fair), XRT +4.0% (15.65x, Fair), JETS +6.0% (11.99x, Cheap).

Notable shifts: the energy complex reaccelerated sharply this run — XLE's YTD jumped from +30.4% to +41.5% as its Q3 partial nearly doubled (+17.6%, from +8.3%), reversing the prior run's pullback, and AMLP followed suit (+20.2%→+25.0%). Gold Miners (GDX) extended its own rally further, Q3 partial +35.8% (from +19.1%) lifting YTD to +19.4% (from +4.8%). Four valuation band crossings this run, versus zero last run: GDX and XRT both moved Cheap→Fair, Health Care (XLV) moved Fair→Elevated (and is itself accelerating, YTD +13.1%), and Cybersecurity (CIBR) moved Elevated→Expensive even as its own momentum faded (Q3 partial +8.9%→+4.2%, YTD +37.3%→+31.4%) — a valuation/momentum divergence worth watching. On the downside, Consumer Discretionary (XLY) reversed back to negative YTD (-1.5%, from +0.8%), joining XLC as the only two sectors underwater — the first run since mid-year with more than one negative-YTD sector.

runs.content:

Notable shifts: a sharp precious-metals/mining rally in the week ended Aug 7 flipped GDX from -13.6% to +4.8% YTD and XME from -2.7% to +11.9% — the largest swings in the tracker — with GLD also turning positive (+0.6%, from -6.3%). That leaves zero sectors in the 'Reversing' bucket for the first time this year. CIBR broke out as the top non-commodity mover, its Q3 partial accelerating to +8.9% (from +2.2%) and pulling YTD from +28.9% to +37.3%. On the flip side, XLE and AMLP — the prior run's clearest momentum leaders — both pulled back this week (XLE +35.0%→+30.4%, AMLP +22.3%→+20.2%), the only two sectors with declining YTD despite a broadly rallying market. XLY crossed into positive YTD (+0.8%, from -2.4%) for the first time in 2026. Data quality note: all 25 P/E figures came back unchanged from the prior run — a clean, stable read with zero valuation band crossings.
